props.title: From Beyond
props.initialSlug: Some dimensions were never meant to be crossed

sections.content: Stuart Gordon's From Beyond (1986) represents the pinnacle of H.P. Lovecraft body horror adaptations, pushing far beyond his earlier Re-Animator (1985). The film follows Dr. Crawford Tillinghast's experiments with the resonator, a machine that stimulates the pineal gland and reveals a horrifying dimension of floating creatures. Like David Cronenberg's Videodrome (1983) and The Fly (1986), it explores body transformation and scientific hubris through groundbreaking practical effects. The film's pulsing purple lighting and visceral practical effects by Mark Shostrom showcase what practical effects could achieve in the 1980s golden age of horror.

sections.content: The film's psychosexual themes and transformation sequences influenced later cosmic horror like In the Mouth of Madness (1994) and Event Horizon (1997). Jeffrey Combs delivers another memorable performance following Re-Animator, establishing himself as the definitive Lovecraft actor. Barbara Crampton's Dr. McMichaels provides a more complex female role than typical '80s horror, anticipating her later genre work in You're Next (2011) and Jakob's Wife (2021).

The practical effects work stands among the best of the era, rivaling Rob Bottin's work in The Thing (1982) and Rick Baker's transformations in An American Werewolf in London (1981). The resonator sequences, with their floating creatures and morphing flesh, demonstrate how practical effects could create truly alien visions before CGI dominance. sections.content: From Beyond helped establish the visual language for Lovecraftian horror on screen, influencing films like Color Out of Space (2019) and The Endless (2017). Its emphasis on the unseen becoming visible through scientific means created a template for cosmic horror that doesn't rely on tentacles and elder gods. Modern filmmakers like Richard Stanley and Justin Benson/Aaron Moorhead continue drawing from its approach to making the incomprehensible tangible.
